label: D-4 part-time work: weekday hour ceiling once the standard is met
appliesTo: D-4-1 language trainees holding a part-time work permit
why: The single figure a student needs to know before signing anything, and the one most often quoted from an out-of-date forum post. Set by administrative guidance, so it moves more readily than the statutory registration deadlines.

history.source: Study in Korea — residence and stay information
history.note: Weekdays during term. Weekends and vacation periods are allowed a higher ceiling, indicated at 25 hours. Students who do not meet the Korean proficiency standard are held to roughly 10 hours a week across weekdays, weekends and vacation alike — so meeting the standard is what doubles the weekday ceiling, not what unlocks work at all.
